RE: DIRECT THE COUNTY EXECUTIVE TO DISBAND THE DATA CENTER ORDINANCE
ADVISORY GROUP

ACTION: APPROVED

WHEREAS, the Data Center Ordinance Advisory Group (DCOAG) has assisted the
County for two years with the development of regulations to address the impacts associated with
data center development; and

WHEREAS, the time and effort volunteered by the DCOAG are commendable; and

WHEREAS, following the data center work session on October 14, 2025, and the
upcoming public hearing on the noise ordinance, the Board will provide the County Executive with
guidance for completing work on the Noise Ordinance, the Zoning Ordinance, and the Design and
Construction Standards Manual; and

WHEREAS, the work of the DCOAG is now completed;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Prince William Board of County
Supervisors hereby directs the County Executive to disband the Data Center Ordinance Advisory
Group and work directly with staff to complete any updates to the Noise Ordinance, the Zoning
Ordinance, and the Design and Construction Standards Manual as it relates to data center
development;

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Prince William Board of Cunty Supervisors
hereby directs the County Attorney’s Office to review the information and recommendations for
any legal issues.

Ayes: Angry, Bailey, Boddye, Franklin

ACTION: APPROVED

WHEREAS, the County is the owner of land at 9525 Hornbaker Road and
11301 Inspiration Court, located in INNOVATION @ Prince William, which the County has
acquired for economic development purposes (the Property); and

WHEREAS, SJP Acquisitions Inc, which is a wholly owned entity of St. John
Properties, Inc. (Purchaser), desires to develop approximately 100,000 square feet of high-
quality flex-tech buildings on the Property; and

WHEREAS, this represents an estimated private sector investment of
$20,200,000; and

WHEREAS, County staff recommends limiting the amount of space in these
flex-tech buildings that can be leased for warehouse, distribution and fulfillment, and
data center uses, and the Purchaser has agreed to these limitations; and

WHEREAS, enacting the limitations and confirming the available square footage
of Land Bays 12 and 13 requires an amendment to the County Declaration; and

WHEREAS, the Purchaser has identified a road bisecting the County-
owned parcels that is shown on the “Master Zoning Plan for Innovation @ Prince
William” dated September 19, 1999, that is Exhibit A to the County Declaration and
requests that the County amend the County Declaration to remove reference to this
road; and

WHEREAS, the County Declaration may be amended by the same
procedure for purposes of amending a proffer under Virginia law and the Board’s
procedures; and

WHEREAS, the Purchaser desires for the County to initiate the amendment
by the same procedure for purposes of amending a proffer under Virginia law and the
Board’s procedures; and

WHEREAS, under Virginia Code § 15.2-1800(B), in general, the Prince
William Board of County Supervisors is required to hold a public hearing prior to the sale
or disposition of County-owned property; and

WHEREAS, County staff recommends approval of this Resolution;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that that the Prince William Board of
County Supervisors hereby initiates an amendment to the County Declaration pursuant to the
same procedure for purposes of amending a proffer under Virginia law and the Board’s
procedures, to include but not limited to limiting the amount of space that can be leased for
warehouse, distribution and fulfillment, and data center uses on parcels addressed as 9525
Hornbaker Road and 11301 Inspiration Court, Manassas, Virginia, removing reference to the
proposed road shown on Exhibit A entitled “Master Zoning Plan for Innovation @ Prince William
County” dated September 19, 1999, and updating the square footage applicable to land bays 12
and 13 to include the area that is part of the “Proposed Road (68’ R/W) which was previously
excluded from those calculations;

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Prince William Board of County Supervisors
hereby authorizes a public hearing to consider approving the Sale Agreement with SJP
Acquisitions, Inc. for the sale of approximately 13.2369 acres of County-owned properties at
9525 Hornbaker Road, and 11301 Inspiration Court, Manassas, Virginia, 20109, for an estimated
price of $4,036,196 to develop approximately 100,000 square feet of high quality flex-tech
buildings, such public hearing to be scheduled for the same meeting as the Board considers the
amendment to the Declaration;

BRENTSVILLE MAGISTERIAL DISTRICT

ACTION: APPROVED

WHEREAS, the County is the owner of land known as INNOVATION @ Prince
William, which the County has acquired for economic development purposes; and

WHEREAS, on December 17, 2024, through Resolution Number 24-820, the Board
of County Supervisors approved the execution of a lease with Patriot Property Group, LLC, for
approximately 2.9 acres of County-owned land located at 9349 Hornbaker Road (GPIN 7695-04-
7375), for use as customer parking in support of the Farm Brew Live campus; and

WHEREAS, this County-owned land is adjacent to NOVA LIVE a highly successful
hospitality and tourism venue attracting an average of 34,000 guests per month, drawing visitors
from across the Mid-Atlantic region; and

WHEREAS, on May 22, 2025, Patriot Property Group, LLC, formally exercised its
two-year renewal option under Paragraph 1(B) of the lease, extending the agreement under the
same covenants, terms, and provisions, including the annual rental amount specified in Paragraph
2(B); and

WHEREAS, the executed lease agreement stipulates that the tenant shall not erect
any temporary or permanent structures other than those required to operate a customer parking
lot without the Landlord’s written permission; and

WHEREAS, the lessee, Villagio Hospitality Group c/o Patriot Property Group, LLC,
has requested authorization for a limited and temporary change of use of the leased parcel from
overflow parking to a special event site for the Taste of NoVA 2025 festival; and

WHEREAS, the Taste of NoVA culinary event, produced by Northern Virginia
Magazine, was initially scheduled to be held at the National Museum of the U.S. Army at Fort
Belvoir, but due to the recent federal government closure, the organizers sought an alternate
location; and

WHEREAS, hosting the 2025 event at NovaLIVE @ Innovation Park represents a
timely opportunity for Prince William County to welcome thousands of visitors, highlight its
hospitality assets, and strengthen its position as a regional destination for dining and culture; and

WHEREAS, the Taste of NoVA event is scheduled for Saturday, October 11, 2025,
and Sunday, October 12, 2025, from 12:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. each day, with setup beginning
Wednesday, October 8 and full restoration completed by Tuesday, October 14; and

WHEREAS, County staff have reviewed and coordinated event logistics to ensure
full compliance with County safety, permitting, and insurance requirements and recommend
approval of this Resolution; and

WHEREAS, due to the time-sensitivity, the County Executive authorized this use of
the County-owned land and now requests ratification by the Board of County Supervisors; and

WHEREAS, County staff recommends approval of this resolution;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Prince William Board of County
Supervisors hereby ratifies the County Executive’s approval of, and authorizes, the limited and
temporary change of use of the County-owned land known as GPIN: 769-5-04-7375, located at

2025;

October 8, 2025, through Tuesday, October 14, 2025, as outlined in the attached request;

to execute all documents that are necessary and/or appropriate to implement this temporary
change of use and effectuate the intent of this resolution, all as approved to form by the County

Rationale: Because it measures sound across nine sound bands, Octave band readings
result in the need to analyze nine numbers, greatly adding to the complexity of the noise
ordinance, infeasibility of enforcement and compliance, and increasing legal risk.
Alternatively, dB(C) is a single number that could be measured without complex
analysis, reducing our dependence on outside consultants and the possibility of legal
challenges. This recommendation is further strengthened when looking at peer counties
and states that have attempted to implement an Octave band system but failed to
maintain long-term enforcement purportedly due to this increased level of complexity.

The specific number limit I am recommending is based on the measurements done by
the DCOAG of non-data center areas, and then using that maximum noise level and
reducing 2 dB, based on 3 dB being the level that results in a noticeable difference to
human ears. That additional 1 dB allows flexibility to account for weather, ambient
natural, traffic and other noise found throughout the county, and other complicating
factors. Based on Wade’s measurement matrix, these numbers would still require some
industrial uses to implement mitigations while avoiding many of the unintended false
positives that would trigger from octave bands.
